CYTOGENETICS AND MOLECULAR GENETICS REPORT
Great Ormond Street Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Patient: 8-month-old male infant
Referral reason: Developmental delay, hypotonia, dysmorphic features suggestive of Prader-Willi syndrome
Clinical features: Poor feeding in neonatal period requiring NG tube, central hypotonia with peripheral hypertonia, almond-shaped eyes, narrow bifrontal diameter, small hands and feet

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Karyotype analysis (G-banding)
2. FISH for 15q11-q13 deletion (SNRPN probe)
3. Methylation-specific MLPA (MS-MLPA) for PWS/AS region
4. SNP microarray analysis

RESULTS

1. KARYOTYPE ANALYSIS
Method: G-banded analysis at 550 band resolution from peripheral blood lymphocytes
Result: 46,XY
No visible deletions or rearrangements detected at this resolution
20 metaphases analysed

2. FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDISATION (FISH)
Probe: SNRPN (15q11.2) with control probe D15Z1
Result: nuc ish del(15)(q11.2q11.2)(SNRPN-)
ABNORMAL - Deletion of SNRPN locus detected
200 interphase nuclei scored: 198 with single SNRPN signal

3. METHYLATION-SPECIFIC MLPA (MS-MLPA)
Kit: SALSA MS-MLPA P245 Microdeletion Syndromes
Result: 
- Copy number: 0.5 ratio for all probes in PWS critical region (MKRN3, MAGEL2, NDN, SNRPN exons)
- Methylation: Abnormal pattern consistent with paternal deletion
- Size: Approximately 5.8 Mb deletion (BP1-BP3)

4. SNP MICROARRAY
Platform: Illumina CytoSNP-850K
Result: arr[GRCh38] 15q11.2q13.1(22,805,313-28,609,476)x1 pat
De novo 5.8 Mb deletion
Parental studies: Neither parent carries deletion (confirmed paternity)

COMBINED INTERPRETATION
The molecular and cytogenetic findings confirm a diagnosis of Prader-Willi syndrome due to a de novo 5.8 Mb paternal deletion of 15q11.2-q13.1, encompassing the PWS critical region. This is a Class I deletion (BP1-BP3), the most common type seen in approximately 70% of PWS deletion cases.

The deletion includes all imprinted genes in the PWS region including MKRN3, MAGEL2, NDN, and the SNORD116 cluster, which are critical for the PWS phenotype.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Referral to specialist PWS multidisciplinary team
2. Growth hormone therapy evaluation when appropriate
3. Nutritional management and monitoring for hyperphagia development
4. Developmental assessment and early intervention services
5. Endocrine evaluation for hypogonadism and other hormone deficiencies
6. Sleep study to assess for sleep-disordered breathing
7. Recurrence risk is <1% for future pregnancies (recommend prenatal testing)

Authorised by: Dr Sarah Johnson, Consultant Clinical Geneticist
